headline: Investment gains fuel profit surge, catastrophe losses bite
summary_short: Cincinnati Financial's Q2 FY2026 net income surged 83.2% y/y to $1.26B ($8.05 diluted EPS) on an $882M after-tax equity fair-value gain, while non-GAAP operating income fell 28% y/y to $224M as the property casualty combined ratio rose to 100.8% on higher catastrophe losses.
summary_long: Net income of $1.26B ($8.05 diluted EPS) was driven mainly by an $882M after-tax gain in unrealized equity fair value plus $657M higher net investment gains and $28M higher investment income, partly offset by a $115M drop in property-casualty underwriting profit. Non-GAAP operating income fell 28% y/y to $224M as the combined ratio rose 5.9pts to 100.8%, including a 2.3pt hit from higher catastrophe losses, primarily in commercial lines (combined ratio +11.2pts). Personal lines improved on lower catastrophe losses. Net written premiums grew 3% on price increases and higher insured exposures. Book value per share rose to $108.64 (+$7.04 in the quarter), and the company declared a $0.94/share dividend. No formal financial guidance was issued in the release.

drivers.explanation: An $882M after-tax gain from unrealized equity fair-value increases plus $657M higher net investment gains and $28M higher investment income, partly offset by a $115M decline in property-casualty underwriting profit.
6% higher earned premiums from price increases and higher insured exposures, 12% higher net investment income, and a $1.308B pretax net investment gain included in total revenues.

Book value per share rose $7.04 in the quarter to $108.64, including $7.09 from investment portfolio and unrealized fixed-maturity gains, partly offset by $0.57 of other items and $0.94 of dividends declared.

Management cited elevated catastrophe losses, especially in Ohio (near 4x the 5-year Q2 average), pushing the combined ratio to 100.8% from 94.9% and cutting non-GAAP operating income 28% y/y to $224M, while investment income was called the main source of quarterly profit.
